note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §6 Pistons, §13.7, Stage 79; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 28) on data/benches/molar_volume.json: 0.50 g of malachite in sulfuric acid gives 2.26 mmol of carbon dioxide, collected in a gas syringe on the flask's mouth: its volume over its moles is a gas's molar volume, about 24 L/mol at the room's temperature and pressure.
title: Experiment: a gas's molar volume

steps.title: Your guess
steps.text: 0.50 g of malachite, Cu2CO3(OH)2 (221 g/mol), gives one carbon dioxide for each formula: 2.26 mmol. How many millilitres of gas will push the syringe out? Type your guess, then click "predict".
steps.why: A mole of any gas takes the same room at the same temperature and pressure (Avogadro).

steps.title: Malachite into the acid
steps.text: Pick up the jar of malachite, then right-click the flask. In the menu, click "tip in".

steps.title: The syringe on its mouth
steps.text: Quickly: pick up the syringe, right-click the flask, and click "on its mouth".
steps.why: Its nozzle in the flask's bung: the gas the acid gives has nowhere to go but into the syringe, which it pushes out at the room's pressure.

steps.title: Collect it
steps.text: Watch the plunger move out as the malachite fizzes away. Speed up time if you like.
steps.why: The air in the flask is pushed into the syringe by the carbon dioxide made under it: the syringe reads what was made.

steps.title: Read it
steps.text: Once the flask is back at the room's temperature, right-click the syringe and click "+ mL".
steps.why: The reaction warmed the flask a little: wait for it to cool, as the volume is read at the room's temperature.

goal.text: every element, mass and energy unchanged

report.label: the gas collected
report.why: 2.26 mmol x 24.06 L/mol at 20 C and 101.3 kPa is 54.4 mL; a little of the carbon dioxide dissolves in the acid instead.

report.label: the molar volume
report.why: The volume over the moles: RT/P is 24.06 L/mol at 20 C and 101.3 kPa, the same for any gas.
